findings.target: outcomes: lutheran--scandinavian, geneva--scottish, geneva--huguenots, geneva--dutch (and, unoutcomed, hieronymian--tridentine, kyiv--ottoman)
findings.issue: The drafters applied the stricter test unevenly to one class of act: a church body adopting another side's confession, catechism, worship order or set text. Four got outcomes: the Uppsala council binding Sweden to the Augsburg Confession, the Scottish General Assembly's order 'according to the Kirk of Geneva', the Paris synod approving the Calvin-drafted confession, and Emden's catechism rule. Two of the same kind were left minor as 'set reading' or 'text taken up': Trent's Vulgate decree and the four patriarchs' 1643 decree that every Orthodox Christian read and receive Mohyla's Confession. The ruling lists translations and set reading among what does not count. A text another body adopts by vote is still a text taken up by the other side. The act that counts is a condemnation, a split, or a rule or settlement imposed or changed by authority (for example Milan's levy, Diamper's ban, the Moscow patriarchate). Separately, the Emden outcome is half about the Heidelberg Catechism, not Geneva, and the link's note never mentions Emden.
findings.fix: Drop the outcome (and outcome_locus) from lutheran--scandinavian, geneva--scottish, geneva--huguenots and geneva--dutch. Record outcome_considered: 'A church body adopted the other side's text or order by its own vote: a text taken up, which the stricter test excludes, as for Trent's Vulgate decree and the patriarchs' 1643 decree.' On geneva--dutch, also drop the Emden source, since the note does not use it. Mark should confirm the class ruling (see escalations_view). If he rules the class counts, add outcomes to hieronymian--tridentine and kyiv--ottoman as well, so that all six are treated alike.

findings.issue: The outcome fails the stricter test. The only act shown is Teresa's own practice of asking the bishop's consent 'according to the decree of the council'. That is a rule followed by one person, a practice taken up. No council, canon or authority's act appears in the listed lines. Trent's decree is mentioned, not quoted. The outcome also repeats the note.
findings.fix: Drop the outcome. outcome_considered: 'Teresa followed a decree of the Council in her own foundations; a practice taken up by one person, with no act of an authority in the listed lines.'

findings.issue: The outcome fails the stricter test, and it says more than its locus shows. Susza (a Uniate writer, 1666) reports only an envoy's words to Smotrytsky: the synod 'censere eam contrariam et impiam'. That is a verbal judgment on one man's book, reported from the other side. It is not a canon or a condemnation of the union or its members. No result that lasted is shown, and Smotrytsky soon went over to the union. 'Smotrytsky's book for the union' is also stronger than the note's 'a book that leaned toward Rome'.
findings.fix: Drop the outcome. outcome_considered: 'An envoy's report of a synod's verdict on one man's book, from the other side; no canon, condemnation of the union or lasting result is shown.'

outcomes_view.reason: The council's mandate that rebaptizers be drowned, and its sentence on Manz, are a law condemning a group (Egli 33701-33706, 33747-33752).
A papal bull abolishing the order is an authority excluding a group (Bullarium 92832-92843). Rewrite the wording (R1-16).
The bull's condemning clause (Mirbt 15502-15506) and Mirbt's summary of the burning order and the penalty clause (15508-15512) show a law condemning a teaching, within 10 lines.
The Uppsala council adopting the Augsburg Confession is a text taken up by vote (R1-05).
The Assembly adopting Geneva's order of worship is a practice taken up by vote (R1-05).
The synod approving a Geneva-drafted confession is a text taken up, and the evidence is an editor's headnote (R1-05).
A council canon condemning the teaching that defines the group (Waterworth 14242-14248).
A split into separate bodies, shown by McGlothlin 2775-2790. That locus must be restored to the census source (R1-01).
Parliament's act ending papal jurisdiction, on pain of banishment, is a law excluding (Knox II 5162-5187).
Treason convictions under statute show a law excluding a group, carried out (Pollen 15381-15402). Rewrite the wording (R1-16).
Emden's catechism rule is a text taken up, half of it the Heidelberg, not Geneva's; the note does not mention it (R1-05).
The Geneva council's sentence of death and the burning of Servetus's books (Calvini Opera 8: 54355-54361, 54713-54717).
A provincial council's new levy, made to carry out Trent's mandate, is a rule set by an authority (Acta 2786-2803). It is a new rule, not a text taken up.
One person's practice under a decree; no authority's act in the listed lines (R1-06).
Two synods condemn and anathematize 'Calvin's heresy' and the Confession's chapters (Lucaris 1645: 2594-2598, 4178-4189).
The bull incorporating the Ruthenian church is a settlement by authority that made a separate body (Harasiewicz 11166-11186).
An envoy's report of a verdict on one book, from the other side; no lasting result (R1-07).
Creating the Moscow patriarchate is a settlement changed by authority (Fletcher 10232-10247; Mouravieff 6040-6070).
Synod decrees condemning the community's books and binding it to Trent (Hough 31939-31955, 32704-32708).

Every relationship the mission-born label names is carried by a regional movement's link, and its dispositions point to those links, so the two-way check is met. The union's synodal charter (Akty IV 13931-13935) and the exarch Nikephoros's circular, cutting the metropolitan off 'as apostates' in the name of the Constantinople throne (15036-15046), are dated rupture documents from both sides. The Kyiv metropolis was subject to that throne. Group G (two 'broke with' links on one side's sources): keep both at Documented, but say so in the notes. ethiopian--jesuits rests on Jesuit histories, which record the expulsion they suffered and quote the emperor's own proclamation (Telles 18963-18967; Lobo 1667-1669). st-thomas--jesuits rests on the community's 1787 document and a Roman Carmelite envoy (Sebastiani 663-666), with no Jesuit letter. The brief says 'ideally from both sides', which is a preference, not a requirement. A Jesuit letter of 1653 and the Susenyos chronicle stay in wants. New, for Mark: the outcome-test class in R1-05. Should a church body adopting another side's confession, catechism or worship order by its own vote count as 'a rule ... changed by an authority', or as 'a text taken up'? The drafters split four to two. My verdict is that it is a text taken up, so drop the four outcomes. Whichever way Mark rules, it must apply to all six links, including Trent's Vulgate decree and the patriarchs' 1643 decree. This interprets his change order, so it is his call.
